claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering is a viable preparation route for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning-driven parameter screening can identify mechanical-alloying and SPS conditions that produce stable RHEA–Cu composites.
The proposed method can produce RHEA–Cu composites at large scale.
The method can overcome the incompatibility associated with a large positive enthalpy of mixing between refractory alloying elements and copper.
The starting material is a powder mixture containing refractory high-entropy-alloy elements and copper.
Mechanical-alloying parameters such as milling time can be optimized to improve subsequent densification.
Machine learning can effectively tune milling time, ball-to-powder ratio, SPS temperature, pressure, and dwell time for this material system.
Mechanical alloying should be performed in an inert or protective environment before SPS.
Optimized mechanical alloying and SPS will produce dense, uniformly distributed RHEA–Cu phases.
Optimized processing will minimize undesired phase segregation in RHEA–Cu composites.
Mechanical alloying and SPS promote rapid, controlled solid-state reactions and consolidation.
Rapid processing reduces unchecked diffusion in the RHEA–Cu system.
Process-variable fine-tuning reduces the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation.
The resulting RHEA–Cu composites will consistently achieve high density and a stable microstructure.
The resulting RHEA–Cu composites will retain mechanical integrity and thermal stability at high temperatures.
Conventional trial-and-error powder metallurgy struggles to control RHEA–Cu phase separation, particularly at scale.
The method is primarily applicable at moderate copper contents and with carefully formulated RHEA compositions.
Success depends on robust machine-learning models, broad parameter datasets, consistent powder quality, and remains unverified at industrial scale.

contradictions.description: Parameter screening inherently anticipates that some tested parameter sets will fail while searching for successful optimized settings, but the falsification rule says failure of any single parameter set falsifies the entire hypothesis.
